en: Machines need power from a substation, the toilet needs water from the pump station (both in a utility room). Cables and pipes are laid in “Utilities” right into the device's cell.

keys: Включите слой «Коммуникации» справа — так видно, что куда подключено.
en: Turn on the “Utilities” layer on the right to see what's connected where.

keys: Здесь — легенда: что значит каждый цвет на карте. Так сразу видно, где прибор без тока или воды.
en: This is the legend: what each color on the map means. You can see at once which device lacks power or water.
Look at the map and press “Next”.

keys: Слой выключается той же кнопкой. Включайте его, когда что-то не работает.
en: The layer turns off with the same button. Turn it on when something doesn't work.

keys: Рук не хватает: строить, носить металл, стоять у станков. Наймём ещё одного человека.
en: You're short of hands: building, hauling metal, running machines. Let's hire one more person.
“People” → “Hiring”: choose a trade, then a person, and “Hire”.

keys: Готово! Новый человек уже в «Сотрудниках» — там весь ваш коллектив: зарплаты, навыки, настроение.
en: Done! The new person is already in “Staff”, where your whole team is: wages, skills, mood.
You can look in there. Then “Next”.
You don't need the People window anymore, close it.

keys: Слева сверху — что сейчас важно: срочные письма, заказы, цели этапа. Щёлкните по строке — откроется нужное окно.
en: Top left is what matters now: urgent letters, orders, stage goals. Click a line to open the right window.

keys: Заглядывайте сюда, когда не знаете, что делать дальше.
en: Look here when you don't know what to do next.

keys: Куда расти — написано в «Целях». Первая цель — 10 заказов и миллион оборота.
en: Where to grow is written in “Goals”. The first goal is 10 orders and a million in turnover.
Open “Goals” with the button at the bottom.

keys: Здесь — цели текущего этапа и прогресс по каждой. Выполните все — завод перейдёт на новый этап.
en: Here are the goals of the current stage and progress on each. Complete them all and the plant moves to a new stage.

keys: «Рейтинг» — звёзды завода. Они складываются из пяти показателей и пересчитываются каждое утро; этапы и сценарии требуют определённого числа звёзд.
en: “Rating” is the plant's stars. They're made up of five indicators and recalculated every morning; stages and scenarios require a certain number of stars.
You can open the section. Then “Next”.
That's it, you can close the window.

keys: Теперь вы знаете главное. Остальное подскажут список задач и письма. Полный справочник по разделам — F1, кнопка «?» вверху или меню паузы.
en: Now you know the essentials. The task list and letters will help with the rest. The full handbook: F1, the “?” button at the top, or the pause menu.

keys: Обучение пройдено! Справка — F1, цели — G.
en: Tutorial complete! Handbook: F1, goals: G.

en: walls and a door: zones only work inside a room

You're the director of a small plant. Take orders, make parts, deliver on time, and grow from a garage box into a town-forming enterprise.

[b]How the production loop works[/b]
• [b]Order[/b]: the sales department accepts requests by itself, the ones the plant can make on time and at a profit.
• [b]Metal[/b]: supply buys it for the order, a truck brings it to the unloading zone, workers carry it to the racks.
• [b]Machine[/b]: a machinist makes the part following its route of operations.
• [b]QC[/b]: an inspector checks the part: good ones go on the pallet, rejects into the bin.
• [b]Shipping[/b]: the finished batch is carried to the shipping zone, and the customer's truck arrives.
• [b]Money[/b]: after loading. Late? You pay a penalty.

Your job isn't to turn parts yourself but to build, hire, answer letters and choose a strategy. This book opens with [b]F1[/b] or the [b]“?”[/b] button at the top; while it's open, the game is paused.

[b]Scenarios[/b]
• [b]Garage[/b]: a box in the industrial zone, an old lathe, three workers and 600,000 ₽ (more on easy, less on hardcore). Teaches the basics with step-by-step hints.
• [b]Greenfield[/b]: a bare lot, a site trailer, a crew of three builders and 1.3 million ₽. The “Shop from scratch”, “Sanitary facilities” and “Job creation” grants help pay for construction.
• [b]Sandbox[/b]: an empty lot, your own money and difficulty, everything open at once, no goals.
In Greenfield and Sandbox the first week is for building: there are no requests. Ready earlier? Use “Start production early” in the task list.

The [b]profile[/b] sets what you get ordered:
• Machine works: many small orders, steady growth.
• Farm machinery: twice the orders in spring; in winter, build up stock.
• Steel structures: huge heavy items, cramped without a crane.
• Pumps and valves: every item goes through the test rig.
• Railway components: pay well, never forgive rejects.
• Machine-tool building: needs almost the whole plant and an engineering office.
• Restricted enterprise: state orders with an advance and military acceptance.

The name (up to 24 characters) and emblem are chosen when you start a new game: 6 shapes, 12 symbols, colors for the background, symbol and border.

• Where it shows: the header at the top, the arch sign over the gate (lit at night), the “Plant sign” (Objects → Decor), the plant newspaper, the stamp on drawings, saves.
• Before registering an LLC the plant is called “Workshop «…»”, after that “LLC «…»”.
• To change it, click the emblem in the header: the plant passport opens.

What to do in the first days:
1. Look at the [b]“What to do” task list[/b] on the left: it suggests the next step.
2. Mark an [b]unloading zone[/b] and a [b]shipping zone[/b] outdoors (Build → Outdoor zones) and put pallets in them: without them there's nowhere to put metal and finished orders.
3. Check that the machine is in a “Workshop” zone and powered, and that there's a [b]rack[/b] for metal, a [b]QC table[/b], a [b]pallet[/b] and a [b]reject bin[/b].
4. Hire the missing people (People → Hiring): a turner, an inspector, a laborer.
5. After that, orders will come by themselves: watch the deadlines in the Orders window and people's mood.

Tip: spend your first money on whatever holds back output the most. The Market shows missed profit, and Production → Downtime shows why machines stand idle.

• [b]“What to do”[/b] (left): task cards. A [color=#e0675a]red[/color] stripe means urgent, [color=#e0aa48]amber[/color] means decide, [color=#7fb6d8]blue[/color] is advice. A click takes you where to deal with it.
• The [b]red banner[/b] under the top bar is the main trouble (wage arrears, negative cash, no tools). Clicking it opens the right window.
• [b]Notifications[/b] at the bottom are clickable: the camera flies to the spot, or a window opens (Finance, Supply, Orders…). Everything is kept in the log (Events → Log).
• Red banners over objects (“No power”, “Broken”, “Not heating”) tell you what to do.
• The production bottleneck is shown in the “Downtime” tab.

In the Garage, the 14-step tutorial walks you through the basics: the screen dims, exactly what to press lights up, and a pulsing frame leads to the target. The camera moves to whatever is being discussed.
• The yellow panel says why and what to do; explanations close with “Got it”.
• First comes the “What we're doing” card with the “order → metal → machine → QC → shipping → money” diagram.
• Missed something? It's all described in this book.

Everything is placed as a [b]blueprint[/b]: you pay first, then workers build it themselves when they're free.
• A blueprint can be canceled (the “Cancel” button) and the money comes back.
• “Construction first” pulls people off hauling and onto building.
• Walls and floors are built from [b]building materials[/b]: bricks, blocks, panels, bags of cement, boxes of tile, rolls of linoleum. The material price is included in the blueprint price; a flatbed truck brings pallets to the unloading zone, and builders carry off as much as they can lift.
• What's coming and when is shown as a line in the Build menu.

[b]Walls[/b]: brick, sand-lime brick, aerated concrete, concrete (cheaper), sandwich panel (builds twice as fast), partition (a cheap way to split a hall into offices).
[b]Floors[/b]: concrete and epoxy (dirt builds up a third slower) for shops; ceramic and blue tile for amenities; linoleum and parquet for offices.
[b]Openings[/b]: windows, wooden, steel and glass doors, gates. Drag them along a wall: several cells in a row become one window, a double door or a sectional gate.
• [b]Ready rooms[/b] (Build): click where to place one and get the floor, walls, doors, furniture and zone at once.

A room is a floor enclosed by walls with a door. Inside it you draw [b]zones[/b] (the “Zones” button, R): drag a rectangle, or click to fill the whole room. One hall can hold several zones.
• The zone color is its group: orange production, yellow storage and shipping, green amenities, blue offices, purple training and union.
• What's missing is shown by a yellow triangle in the middle of the zone.
• Heat, light, noise, ventilation, the overhead crane, cameras and the extinguisher are shared by the whole hall.
• [b]Zones are required[/b]: machines only work in a “Workshop”, toilets in a “Toilet”, lockers in a “Locker room”, people eat in a “Canteen”, and the substation and pump station only work in a “Utility room”. An object outside its zone is marked with a triangle, and its card has a “Zone it” button.

• [b]Workshop[/b]: a machine or workbench.
• [b]Storage[/b]: a rack, pallet or bin.
• [b]Locker room[/b]: 2 locker places and a bench.
• [b]Canteen[/b]: a dining table, 2 chairs, a fridge or microwave.
• [b]Toilet[/b]: a toilet and a sink (and water). [b]Shower room[/b]: a shower stall and a sink.
• [b]Break room[/b]: a bench or sofa, a cooler or kettle.
• [b]Tool crib[/b]: a tool cabinet.
• [b]Utility room[/b]: a substation or pump station. [b]Compressor room[/b]: a compressor. [b]Boiler room[/b]: a gas boiler.
• [b]Office[/b] and department offices: an office desk (+ their own item: a safe, a drafting board, a planning board…).
• [b]Classroom[/b]: two school desks and a chalkboard. [b]Union office[/b]: a desk and a union board.
• [b]Dormitory[/b]: a bunk bed and a locker. [b]First aid post[/b]: a couch, a medicine cabinet, a sink.
• [b]Director's office[/b]: a director's desk.
Outdoors: an [b]unloading zone[/b] and a [b]shipping zone[/b].

Build → Rooms: workshop 10×6, storage 6×4, office 4×3, toilet 3×2, canteen 5×4, locker room 4×3, utility room 5×3 (with a substation and a pump station).
• Click the ground and the floor, walls, doors, furniture and lights are ordered; the zone is marked automatically once it's built. Sizes are interior, without walls.
• You can place one right against another room: the [b]shared wall[/b] isn't built or paid for.
• Floor and walls are chosen in the menu (“Floor: …”, “Walls: …”), and the price is recalculated.

The “Plan” button (V): draw your future plant on tracing paper: walls, floors, zones, machines, ready-made rooms. Free, and workers don't touch the plan.
• The bar at the top shows the estimate, “Approve plan”, “Erase plan”, “Done”.
• “Approve” turns the plan into blueprints; trees in the way are marked for felling, zones and furniture appear by themselves once the walls are built.
• Demolition in plan mode erases the plan. Outside plan mode the plan is shown faintly.

A room has a [b]comfort level[/b] of 1–5 stars: windows, a good floor, electric light, plants and decor (palm, aquarium, rug, bookcase, TV, banner, safety stand…). A higher level means better mood. A big shop needs more decor.
• Machines shed [b]chips[/b] and people track in dirt: mood drops, people slip on chips, sanitary inspectors fine you.
• [b]Cleaners[/b] tidy up, and laborers too if it gets really dirty.
• Chips are swept into a [b]chip bin[/b] (4,000 ₽, 300 kg); on Fridays the scrap truck pays for chips and rejects.
• The “Cleanliness” overlay shows dirt and room stars.

• [b]Demolish[/b] (X): walls, floors, objects. The starting fence can be demolished too.
• [b]R[/b] rotates an object while placing it; a placed one with the “Rotate” button on its card.
• Dismantled items are carried in crates to the equipment store. Place the same object again and it's taken from there for free; extras can be sold (Production → Equipment store).
• Clicking any structure opens its card with a description and a demolish button.

Trees and bushes get in the way of placing objects.
• Demolish → tree: a builder cuts it down.
• You can draw a floor or wall where a tree stands right away; it will be cut down first.
• Trees sway in the wind, turn yellow in autumn and stand bare with snow in winter.

A 2×2 [b]transformer substation[/b] (120,000 ₽) in a [b]utility room[/b] is the only power source: 40 kW for the whole plant, no contracts.
• Up to 9 [b]battery cabinets[/b] (40,000 ₽) go right next to it (corners count too): each adds +20 kW, up to 220 kW total.
• Cable (150 ₽ per cell) runs right [b]into the socket cell[/b] of an object (the yellow icon on the layer), and into any cell of the substation.
• Cable is laid as a blueprint by an electrician (or a builder or laborer). Until a cell is laid, no power flows through it.
• A load bar sits over the substation. Overload trips the breaker; an electrician or worker resets it.
• Electricity costs 7.5 ₽ per kWh. In the Garage and Greenfield the utility room is already built.

Fixtures under the ceiling: a light bulb (small warm circle), a fluorescent fixture (bigger, cool), an industrial high-bay lamp (the biggest), a street lamp.
• A fixture connects by itself if a cable runs within 3 cells.
• Windows also give light in the daytime.
• In the dark people work slower and get injured more often. The “Lighting” overlay shows dark spots.

A 2×2 [b]pump station[/b] (90,000 ₽) in a utility room, powered: one per plant supplies water to every fixture, however many.
• Pipes (120 ₽ per cell) run into the cells of toilets, sinks, showers and the test rig.
• Without water a toilet and sink can't be used.
• Builders lay pipes from a blueprint.

• A [b]radiator[/b] (6,500 ₽) heats about 22 cells of a room.
• Radiators only heat if an [b]electric heating boiler[/b] (48,000 ₽) is working: it goes right next to the pump station (no more than one cell away) and needs power.
• Or your own [b]boiler room[/b]: a gas boiler (260,000 ₽) in a separate room heats up to 16 radiators connected by pipe. Heat at half the price, and heating-main failures don't matter.
• Heating is needed when it's below +10 °C outside. People are comfortable at about +21 °C; below +15 it's cold.
• Heat-treatment furnaces warm the shop by themselves. The “Temperature” overlay shows heat by room.

Welding, painting, furnaces and casting give off smoke: without extraction a room is stuffy, people get angry and work slower, and sanitary inspectors fine you.
• An [b]exhaust fan[/b] (32,000 ₽, powered) pulls air from its own room and, through ducts (650 ₽ per cell), from others, up to 80 cells in total.
• An [b]exhaust hood[/b] over a welding station or booth removes three quarters of the smoke at the source.
• The “Utilities” overlay shows the air in rooms.

A [b]screw compressor[/b] (96,000 ₽, 7.5 kW) gives 8 atm to four users at once.
• A paint booth without air paints by brush, 1.5× slower.
• Assembly benches with pneumatic tools are 20% faster.
• Air line: 380 ₽ per cell. The compressor is noisy, so put it in a separate compressor room.

• [b]Broken wire[/b]: the cable sparks, and there's no power further down the line.
• [b]Burst pipe[/b]: a puddle, and toilets and sinks past the burst are dry.
A letter offers a choice: an [b]emergency crew[/b] (9,000 ₽ for a wire, 12,000 ₽ for a pipe, fixed within an hour) or your own people: the damaged piece appears among the blueprints, and any free worker replaces it out of turn.
Clicking the failure spot opens a card with an “Emergency crew” button.

The column of icons on the right edge:
• Zones: what's where and what's missing.
• Utilities: cable, plumbing, air, ventilation.
• Lighting, Temperature, Cleanliness.
• Foot traffic: where people walk most; put storage and lockers closer there.
• Machine load: working, idle, rejects (needs a planning office).
• Crews and security: crew areas, cameras and posts.
Click to turn on, again to turn off; the legend is a card at the bottom left.

Each machine does its own process, and each needs its own specialist:
• Turning: a turner; milling and drilling: a miller.
• Welding: a welder; assembly: an assembler.
• Heat treatment: a heat treater; painting: a painter.
• Casting: a caster; stamping: a press operator.
• Rig testing: an inspector.
• CNC machines: a CNC operator.
The machine passport (its card and the tooltip in the Objects menu): part size, speed, rejects, batch, consumption, required grade. Machines only work in a “Workshop” zone and when powered.

Products come [b]small[/b] (pins, bushings, brackets, bolts), [b]medium[/b] (shafts, housings, gears, flanges) and [b]large[/b] (railcar axles, beams, trusses, pumps).
• A machine takes parts up to its size: benchtop and small machines only small stuff; 1K62/16K20/6R12 small and medium; heavy ones (1M63, 6R13, 2M55, pit and bogie furnaces, the paint line) any size.
• A large machine does large parts first.
• No machine of the right size? Sales writes “turning (for large parts)” in the refusal.
• Heavy parts are carried one at a time; in a hall with an overhead crane, the crane moves them.

• [b]TV-4[/b]: 65,000 ₽, benchtop, small stuff only, barely uses power.
• [b]1A616[/b]: small parts faster than the 1K62.
• [b]1K62[/b]: 160,000 ₽, old and indestructible: small and medium parts.
• [b]16K20[/b]: 240,000 ₽, the most common: faster and more precise than the 1K62.
• [b]1M63[/b]: 460,000 ₽, heavy 4×1: railcar axles and big shafts, needs a grade 2+ turner.
Small fasteners (M16 bolt, nut, stud) run on any lathe, even the TV-4.

[b]Mills[/b]: 6T80 and 6R10 (small), 6R12, 6R82 (horizontal), 6R13 (heavy): housings, brackets, gear teeth.
[b]Drills[/b]: NS-12, 2N118, 2N135, 2N150, radial 2M55 (2×2, for large parts).
Both processes are run by a miller; cutting tools wear 1.5× faster on milling and twice as slowly on drilling as on turning.

[b]Welding[/b] (consumes welding wire and gas): stick welder VD-306 (cheap, slow), MIG welder PDG-251, spot welder MT-1928 (fast, more rejects), welding station, rig with positioner. Frames, trusses, beams. Needs extraction.
[b]Assembly[/b]: assembler's bench, press P-6326, assembly bench, assembly rig, assembly line (almost twice as fast). Assemblies are built from your own parts; with compressed air, 20% faster.

[b]Heat[/b]: SNOL muffle furnace (3 small parts), induction hardener (two at a time, three times faster, no smoke), chamber furnace (batch of up to 6), pit furnace (8 large), bogie furnace (12). A furnace hardens a batch by itself and warms the shop.
[b]Painting[/b] (consumes primer and paint): paint table, small booth, powder booth (−40% paint, fewer rejects), paint booth, paint line. A booth needs compressed air, otherwise they paint by brush.

[b]Casting[/b]: the “Casting shop” research (after “Flange”). Induction furnace IST-0.16 (2×2) and casting line LU-2 (3×2, from “Medium business”): they melt the charge (140 ₽), the caster pours it into flasks; consumes molding sand. A lot of power, hot and smoky.
[b]Stamping[/b]: the “Stamping” research. Crank press KD2126 and stamping press KB235: from 2 mm strip in one stroke. The loudest area: without earplugs people get angry.
Products: cast cover, cast gearbox housing, spring washer (by the hundred), mounting clamp, bent bracket.

A separate section of the Objects menu.
• Domestic: the [b]16A20F3[/b] lathe (1.6 million ₽) and the [b]65A60[/b] machining center, from the “CNC lathe” and “Machining center” research.
• Imported: Sidway, Mayday, Panthera, Hangan, Hartwood, Minger, from the “Imported CNC” research.
• 1.7–2.2× faster and more precise than conventional machines, and quieter. Needs a [b]CNC operator[/b] (skill 4+); they come to interviews as soon as the plant has such a machine.
• The signal tower glows green while the machine works.

Complex products follow a route of several operations: turning → milling → drilling → heat treatment or painting → assembly.
• Between operations parts are [b]work in progress[/b]: put up a WIP rack (9,000 ₽).
• Every product's route: Production → Product routes.
• A machine needs a [b]changeover[/b] (about 20 minutes) when it switches product or operation. A planning office halves changeovers, and “Batches” and “Lean production” cut them further.

• Machines wear out with use. A worn one is serviced by a turner, fitter or handy worker: about 40 minutes and 3,500 ₽ for cutters and spare parts.
• Below 30% condition a machine may break down: repair takes about 3 hours and 22,000 ₽ (property insurance returns 80%).
• [b]Preventive maintenance[/b] (Production → Machines): service earlier, from 75%.
• Fitters repair fastest of all; the “machine care” improvement proposal slows wear by 25%.

• A [b]band saw[/b] (85,000 ₽) cuts bar stock into blanks in advance: the first operation on a ready blank is 20% faster.
• A [b]CNC setter[/b] sets machines up ahead of the next operation and services them, so machinists don't stand idle.
• A [b]fitter[/b] at the fitter's bench reworks rejects, hacksaws blanks until you have a saw and repairs machines quickly.

Supply restocks consumables by itself:
• Cutting tools: 6,000 ₽ per set for 40 operations (turning, milling, drilling).
• Welding wire and gas: 3,500 ₽ (12 units).
• Primer and paint: 4,500 ₽ (30 units).
• Molding sand: 2,400 ₽ for 20 flasks.
• PPE: 7,500 ₽ for 5 kits.
In a [b]tool crib[/b] (a zone with a tool cabinet) cutters wear a quarter slower. No tools and no money: machines stop, people get angry.

Production → [b]Downtime[/b]: every machine that isn't working right now and the reason in plain words: broken, no power or cable, sealed, worn, outside a workshop, no water, no task, no consumable, no one to run it, machinist off shift, output full, no metal, waiting for blanks.
• Three groups: “Needs your attention”, “Will stop soon”, “Normal waiting”.
• Clicking a line shows the machine and opens its card.
• The [b]bottleneck[/b] is the process holding back output the most; it shows in the “Downtime” tab.

A [b]QC table[/b] (26,000 ₽): the inspector checks every part. Good ones go on the pallet, rejects into the reject bin.
• Rejects are born at the machine: fewer with an experienced worker, on a precise machine, under a foreman's eye.
• QC catches some of the rejects, more the higher the inspector's skill.
• A missed reject goes to the customer: a [b]complaint[/b] means a refund and a reputation hit. A lawyer can dispute a complaint.

• Rejected parts sit in the [b]reject bin[/b] (2,500 ₽).
• A [b]fitter[/b] takes a part from the bin, fixes it (chance depends on skill) and takes it back to QC. “Rework cards” save 15% more.
• On Fridays the scrap truck takes rejects and chips and pays for the scrap.
• A reject has to be made again: the order waits, more metal is bought.

A hydraulic rig (180,000 ₽) with pressure gauges and a flaw detector. Pumps, valves, axles and state-order items are tested here; run by an inspector, needs water.
The “Pumps and valves” profile can't deliver a single item without a rig.

• Experienced machinists and the grade exam.
• A section foreman: 15% fewer rejects.
• “Statistical process control”: 25% fewer rejects, QC catches 10% more.
• The “inspection gauge” improvement proposal: 20% fewer rejects for that part.
• CNC machines, the powder booth, “Welding jigs”.
• Don't overuse rush jobs: 1.5× more rejects. Worn machines, fatigue and bad mood also cause rejects.

Management → ISO 9001 (after the “ISO 9001” step in Development). Requirements: QC, quality of 65%+, an engineering office, a workplace assessment, a safety briefing and two weeks without complaints.
• The audit costs 120,000 ₽, the certificate lasts half a year (84 game days), then a surveillance audit.
• With the certificate you get more requests and contracts, and customers hardly leave even at premium prices.

Orders are taken by the [b]sales department[/b] by itself: requests arrive every morning, and sales accepts those the plant can make on time and at a profit, judging by the busiest process (turning, milling, QC…), and buys the metal itself.
• Requests without free capacity wait a day and a half: when a machine frees up, sales takes them.
• Orders → In progress → New orders: Take / Don't take pauses intake.
• Each order has a [b]priority[/b] (urgent ones are made first) and a GOST [b]drawing[/b] of the part.

The Orders window: how much to risk deadlines (“With margin”, “Normal”, “Tight”, the last with the “Tight scheduling” step), from what margin to take orders (5, 15 or 25%), what to keep in your range.
The Market tab: what customers ask for, this week's prices, your capacity and [b]missed profit[/b], how much you lose without the right machine or person. It's a hint for what to build next. With an accountant you see margins; with a planning office, whether you'll make it in time.

• Lateness costs a 5% penalty per day (up to 30% of the amount); after 3 days the order fails.
• Every overdue day lowers reputation; after 2 days the customer comes to sort it out: a 10% penalty and +4 days, a promise to deliver within 2 days, or cancellation.
• [b]Extension[/b]: “+2 d” in Orders → In progress is a call to the customer: the deadline moves two working days later for a 12% discount and a little reputation. Once per order; state orders can't be extended.

The first order for a new complex product (several operations or assembly) is small, with double the time and no penalty. The shop masters the product risk-free; a failed trial batch hits reputation three times more gently.

[b]Contracts[/b] (the “Contracts” step): big customers offer supplies for 4–8 weeks at a 10–25% markup once every week or two. Often for a product you have no equipment for: you get a week or two before it starts. Miss a weekly batch and you're fined; miss two and the contract is terminated.
[b]Annual agreement[/b] (from “Medium business”, reputation 55+): 24 weeks, bigger batches, a 6–13% markup, a 10% advance. It tolerates two misses; the third means termination, a 10% penalty on the undelivered part and −15 reputation. Fulfilled: an 8% bonus and +12 reputation.

• From the “Medium business” stage, export orders and state orders arrive.
• The “Tenders” step (legal department): state orders with [b]military acceptance[/b], a 50% advance and a third higher price. Needs an LLC and a staffed gatehouse.
• Military acceptance inspects regularly, and items go through the test rig.
• “Hot” orders and tenders are decided by the director, by letter.

Orders → Competitors (needs a sales manager). Our [b]market share[/b] depends on capacity, quality, deadlines, reputation, prices and ISO 9001.
• [b]Dumping[/b]: prices 10% lower, a third more requests, thinner margins.
• [b]Market[/b]: normal prices.
• [b]Premium[/b]: prices 12% higher, fewer requests.
Competitors start price wars, expand, poach experienced workers and sometimes go bankrupt; their equipment can be bought at auction for 40% of the price.

Production → Metal & consumables. Materials: St45 round bar (260 ₽), S27 hex bar (450 ₽), 40Kh round bar (780 ₽), 8 mm plate (520 ₽), housing forging (1,400 ₽), 40×40 profile (380 ₽), charge (140 ₽), 2 mm strip (160 ₽).
• The metal price shifts every day, sometimes in jumps: cheap, buy ahead; expensive, buy only for orders.
• Stock: “Orders only”, “Small” (+20%), “Large” (+50%).
• With a buyer: supplier choice (bulk 10–23% cheaper) and a price chart.
• Short of money? The supplier ships on credit with two weeks' deferral (+5%), within a limit.

[b]Required[/b]: Build → Outdoor zones → “Unloading”. Trucks bring metal, building materials and equipment crates here, and workers carry them from here to racks and install spots.
• Metal and blanks go on [b]stock pallets[/b] (about 300 ₽) in the unloading zone; put several there right away.
• Mark the zone by the gate, close to storage: a shorter path means faster unloading.
• If you remove or move the zone, goods on the floor are carried to the new one.
• If the driver didn't wait for unloading, the cargo is left in numbered stacks; clicking a stack opens the “Cargo on the ground” card.

[b]Required[/b]: Build → Outdoor zones → “Shipping”. Finished parts of an order are brought here while the customer's truck is on its way; money comes after loading.
• Put [b]finished goods pallets[/b] (300 ₽ each) in the zone: good parts are stacked on them.
• Parts go to shipping right away, without waiting for the whole batch.
• If the zone is full you'll get a notification: extend it, or orders will wait in storage.

• [b]Metal rack[/b] (9,000 ₽): two shelves of 12 bars.
• [b]WIP rack[/b] (9,000 ₽): parts between operations.
• [b]Finished goods pallet[/b]: 16 parts that passed QC; orders are loaded from here.
• [b]Reject bin[/b]: QC puts rejects here.
• [b]Chip bin[/b]: 300 kg of chips.
• [b]Storage[/b]: a room with racks; removed equipment is kept there too.

• A [b]hand cart[/b] (15,000 ₽): a laborer carries 12 units a trip instead of 6.
• An [b]electric forklift[/b] (950,000 ₽): 24 units and a third faster. Only an experienced loader drives it (loading 6+).
• An [b]overhead crane 3.2 t[/b] (380,000 ₽): click inside a shop and the runways go along the walls, the bridge from wall to wall. The crane carries a heavy part, a person drives it with a pendant; without a crane it's dragged, 40% slower.
• “Kanban”: loaders carry 50% bigger batches.

• [b]Van[/b]: small deliveries and crates.
• [b]Truck[/b]: big batches of metal (18+ units).
• [b]Semi[/b]: machines, substations and export.
• [b]Flatbed[/b]: pallets of building materials.
• [b]Scrap collector's truck[/b]: takes scrap metal on Fridays.
Cargo is visible in the truck bed; deliveries go to the unloading zone.

A bought machine or furniture comes by van: big items in several crates (one person carries each), small things (a chair, a plant, a kettle) are carried by hand. When all the crates are at the spot, the object is assembled.
A machine from 40,000 ₽ can be leased (the toggle in Objects).

People → Hiring. “Who are we looking for?”: search trades by text and by group (at machines, workers, services and security, engineers and office), each with its number of candidates.
• “Find: Turner · 3,500 ₽”: a job ad for the trade brings new candidates.
• Hire for your orders: wages are paid for every shift, even with nothing to do.
• With an HR department: 6 candidates instead of 4, all traits and mood shown in numbers, ads half price.
• Out-of-towners arrive on Mondays if the dormitory has free bunks.

• Two shifts: 1st from 8:00 to 17:00, 2nd from 17:00 to 02:00 (night hours +20%).
• Shift, wage and bonus are changed on the person's card.
• “Bonus for all” (3,000 ₽), “Wages +5%” and “Market wages” are in People → Staff.
• Staff: search by name, trade, grade, traits; filters “Unhappy”, “Idle”, “Newcomers”, “Absent”.

• People come in their own clothes and change into overalls at a locker (a double locker counts as two places).
• They have lunch 4 hours into the shift, for 45 minutes; they use the toilet; smokers take smoke breaks.
• Tired people rest in the break room.
• After the shift machinists, welders, painters and laborers take a [b]shower[/b]; with no shower or all stalls busy, they leave dirty and unhappy.

Mood is made of [b]thoughts[/b]: where they had lunch, where they changed, what the toilet is like, enough light, warmth, what the pay is, who they work with.
• Good mood means faster work; bad means slower; below 22 they skip work, below 12 for several days they quit.
• [b]What matters[/b] (card → Overview): five bars: living conditions, money, work, team, home. Hover to see what makes them up.
• Icons over their heads show needs and emotions.

Everyone has 1–2 traits: Workaholic, Lazybones, Smoker, Grumbler, Joker, Neat Freak, Handy, Early Bird, Night Owl, Drinker, Foodie, Tireless, Penny-Pincher, Old School, Curious, Born Mentor, Life of the Party, Quarrelsome, Innovator, Quiet One, Trainee, Pilferer, Activist.
Without an HR department you don't see all of a candidate's traits.

• Everyone has skills by trade; a skill grows with work.
• Courses raise a skill, while a [b]grade[/b] comes from an exam (card → “Exam”): on shift the person makes a test part and takes it to the foreman. The chance depends on skill, the foreman and mood.
• Pass: a grade and a request for a raise; fail: a retake in a week.
• Engineers have a category (II, I, lead) instead of a grade.

People → Training: grade-up courses (+2 to a skill) and second-trade courses (access to other machines).
• In your own [b]classroom[/b] (two desks, a board) it's cheap and the person studies during their shift; at a training center it's pricier and they're away for several days.
• A [b]mentor[/b] triples a trainee's growth at the machine but works a bit slower himself.
• [b]Vocational school[/b] (the “Vocational school link” step): trainees are cheap and learn twice as fast; take the best onto the staff.

• People who work side by side and chat on smoke breaks and at lunch make friends. A friend on shift makes work more fun, a foe makes it worse.
• Those who don't get along quarrel; a quarrel sometimes ends in a fight: onlookers gather, and a guard or the foreman breaks it up.
• After a fight the director gets a letter: reprimand both, fire the instigator or move them to different shifts.

• [b]Indexation[/b]: once a quarter prices rise by 4%, and so do market wages. A letter: index for everyone, only for workers, or for no one, and then “they pay less than anywhere else”.
• [b]Age[/b]: once a year everyone gets older; after 50 they tire faster.
• A year at the plant makes a “plant veteran”, respected by all.
• [b]Retirement[/b]: women from 55, men from 60; you can persuade them to stay or see them off with honors.

• Select a person and [b]right-click[/b] a machine and they go work there; right-click a cell and they go there. When done, they return to their usual work.
• Click a person for the menu above them; “Take Control” makes them drop everything and wait for commands. Click a blueprint, machine, cargo or spot and choose “Do it now”. Right-click does the same without the menu.
• “Release” or Esc returns them to their usual work. You can control one person at a time.

Machines, QC tables, band saws and benches are assigned to people (in the morning free places go to those who have none).
• The owner works first; if they're off shift, on sick leave or busy, anyone qualified steps in.
• To change the owner: object card → “Change…”.

“Dismiss” opens a choice of reason: by mutual agreement (compensation), redundancy (severance pay), for absenteeism, for theft, “can't cope”, no reason.
• Each one is marked “lawful” or “no grounds” with an explanation.
• Without grounds: a lawsuit (after a week ≈15 wages, half that with a lawyer), a complaint to the labor inspectorate, and reputation and everyone else's mood drop.

People → Crews (K). A crew leader gets +10% pay and speeds up their crew by 3–6%.
• Assign a shop to a crew and people take work on their own machines first.
• “Form automatically” splits everyone up by shop.
• The “Crews and security” overlay shows the areas.

A foreman hands out shift tasks and keeps discipline; he leads up to 12 people of his shift.
• The shift works 8–15% faster, with 15% fewer rejects and half the absences.
• Without a foreman, a shift of more than 10 people works 10% worse.
• Needs a foreman's booth with an office desk.
Shop manager: rush jobs and overtime

A shop manager: +5% speed for all workers and the director's orders:
• [b]Rush job[/b]: +25% speed, but more rejects (×1.5) and fatigue.
• [b]Overtime[/b]: the shift is 2 hours longer at time and a half.
The orders are a line above the Development tree.

People → Shift schedule, in 15-minute slots: a planning meeting (+3% speed for the shift), lunch (at least 30 minutes, otherwise a fine), a tea break, cleanup at the end of the shift.
Crews can get their own schedule, meaning shorter canteen queues.
Socialist competition and the Board of Honor
The “Socialist competition” step: on Fridays the best crew (operations per person) gets a pennant, +mood and +3% speed for a week. The Board of Honor shows the leading workers of the month.

A trade union appears once you have 8 or more workers (or with the “Union” step, 40,000 ₽).
• The union committee proposes a collective agreement, warns about strikes in advance and gives people more patience.
• A broken collective agreement angers everyone.

If people stay unhappy for a long time, they strike: all workers go to the gatehouse with placards and make a demand. Meet it, bargain or wait: you decide by letter. Raise the mood in advance: market wages, amenities, lunches.

Pilferers carry off metal and consumables when leaving the shift.
• A [b]gatehouse with turnstiles[/b] (45,000 ₽) goes right into the fence: everyone comes and goes through the turnstiles. A guard on shift sits in the booth: with him more than half are caught, and bag checks only work with him.
• [b]Security cameras[/b] (14,000 ₽) deter and record.
• On Fridays there's a stocktake. Someone who's caught can be lawfully fired for theft.

Every specialist needs an [b]office desk[/b] (18,000 ₽) in their department's office (with the right item: a safe for accounting, a drafting board for engineering, a planning board for the planning office…) or in a shared office, where they work 30% worse.
The second Development steps need the department's own office.

• [b]Section foreman[/b]: shift speed and discipline.
• [b]Shop manager[/b]: rush jobs and overtime.
• [b]Accounting[/b]: 5% tax instead of 6%, reports, loans at 17%; required once you have more than 8 people.
• [b]Supply[/b]: suppliers, bulk 10–23% cheaper.
• [b]Planning office[/b]: plan, priorities, half the changeovers, “on time?”.
• [b]HR department[/b]: more candidates, traits and mood in numbers.
• [b]Engineering office[/b]: research.
• [b]Sales department[/b]: competitors, pricing policy, +10% requests.
• [b]Workplace safety[/b]: −15% injuries, your own N-1 report.
• [b]Legal department[/b]: appealing fines (60% instead of 40%), complaints, tenders.

Window sections a department is responsible for are locked until you have it. Without an accountant, only money and recent transactions; without an HR officer, mood is shown in words; without a buyer, no metal price chart and no buying ahead; without a planning office, no plan and no “on time?”.
The lock says which office to build and whom to hire, and “What to do” says which department is next.
A room with linoleum and a [b]director's desk[/b] (35,000 ₽). Without it Development steps can't be researched: the director studies them from here, one at a time, for money and a few days.

Management → Chief engineer suggests what matters most right now: bottlenecks, deadlines, breakdowns, mood, money, metal.
• Preventive maintenance turns on by itself for new machines; a utilities summary: power, air, water.
• When wages eat more than 70% of revenue, he'll point out which machinists stand idle.

Six stages: [b]Garage[/b] (1–5 people) → [b]Workshop[/b] (5–15) → [b]Small business[/b] (15–30) → [b]Medium[/b] (30–50) → [b]Large plant[/b] (50–100) → [b]Town-forming[/b] (100+).
• Each opens new machines, shops and departments; goals are in the Goals window (G).
• From “Workshop”, the next stage needs two mandatory goals and any two of four roads: volume (turnover 2 → 5 → 12 → 30 million ₽), quality, people or town.
The 1–5 star rating is made up of output and deadlines, quality, safety, people's mood and finances. Goals → Rating shows what each star is made of. “Large plant” on the quality road needs 4 stars.

Management → Development & departments: eight branches of three steps each: finance, HR, production, planning, market, engineering, law & safety, town (plus land).
• The first step of a branch opens when you hire a specialist.
• The director researches the rest from the director's office, one at a time, for money and a few days.
• “Workshop” permits second steps, “Small business” third steps.
• Steps are held by people: fire the holder and the step goes dark until a new one is hired.

• Cost accounting: 120,000 ₽, 3 days: margins and cash forecast.
• Bank & leasing: 300,000 ₽: loans up to 3 million at 14%, leasing, insurance.
• Vocational school link: 100,000 ₽: trainees and out-of-towners.
• Talent pool: 250,000 ₽: “may quit” flag, auto-replacement.
• Socialist competition: 250,000 ₽: the Board of Honor, twice the improvement proposals.
• Batches: 120,000 ₽: operations 30% faster. Tight scheduling: 300,000 ₽.
• Contracts: 350,000 ₽: contracts and export (reputation 60+).
• ISO 9001: 300,000 ₽. Tenders: 400,000 ₽.
• Union: 40,000 ₽. Social services: 150,000 ₽: stove, serving line, medical room, dormitory. Patronage: 350,000 ₽: kindergarten, House of Culture, radio.

The neighboring lots beyond the fence are for sale: a [b]“For sale”[/b] sign hangs over them in a light haze. Click the sign to open Development → “Land”.
• The east lot (from “Workshop”), the west lot (from “Small business”), the back yard (from “Medium”). Price: 1,200 ₽ per cell.
• A bought lot becomes yours: the old fence can be torn down.
• The lots have old buildings on them, a warehouse, a former sawmill, a row of garages: walls and floor are already there, it's dirty inside, and light and water are up to you.
Achievements are shared across all games: the list is in the Goals window and in the main menu. They don't count in Sandbox.

Management → Research (T). The tree opens when you have a [b]process engineer[/b] on staff (an “Engineering office”: an office desk and a drafting board).
• The engineer earns research points during working hours; the chosen project opens once there are enough points.
• Branches: processes, automation, fitting, products, management, social. Lines show what must be researched first.

• High-speed cutting: turning, milling and drilling operations 15% faster.
• Heat treatment modes: the furnace heats a batch 25% faster.
• Efficient nesting: metal 8% cheaper.
• Welding jigs: welding 20% faster, 30% fewer rejects.
• CNC lathe → Machining center → Imported CNC.
• Fitting: rework cards, fitter's tooling.

• Flange: from a forging, turning and drilling, good demand.
• Spur gear: turning, gear hobbing, hardening.
• Gearbox: an assembly of a splined shaft, two gears, a housing and bushings, painted. The most expensive.
• Casting shop and Stamping: new processes and products.
The first order for a new complex product is a trial batch.

• 5S: everyone 5% faster, people like the order.
• Kanban: loaders carry 50% more.
• Statistical process control: 25% fewer rejects.
• Lean production: changeovers twice as short, another +5% speed.
• Workplace exercises: people tire 15% slower.
• Set lunches: lunch pleases more.
• Classroom: skills grow twice as fast.

• Income: payment for orders after loading, contracts, scrap metal.
• Expenses: wages for every shift, metal and consumables, electricity (7.5 ₽ per kWh), heating, construction, inspections and fines.
• [b]Tax[/b]: 6% of revenue every Friday (5% with accounting). With more than 8 people on staff and no accounting, the tax office fines you.
• The Garage start is 600,000 ₽ (the calm five-year plan +30%, the wild nineties −15%). For the first two weeks regular customers pay a 30% advance.

Finance → Loans & leasing. The bank gives loans from the “Workshop” stage: at 22%, at 17% with accounting, and up to 3 million ₽ at 14% with the “Bank & leasing” step.
[b]Leasing[/b]: a machine from 40,000 ₽: 20% up front, the rest in payments over 12 weeks (+18%).

Finance → Insurance (the “Bank & leasing” step). Premiums are paid on Mondays.
• [b]Property[/b]: 80% of machine repair costs and fire damage.
• [b]Liability[/b]: half of penalties, complaints and contract fines.
• [b]Accident[/b]: the whole compensation under an N-1 report.

Finance → Grants are mini-quests: apply for a support program, meet the conditions (equip a shop or canteen, create jobs), and after an inspection your expenses are reimbursed.
Programs appear depending on your situation: have a canteen, “A bigger canteen”; cash in the red, “Crisis support”; smoky welding and painting, “Clean air in the shop”. You'll be notified about a new suitable program.

• Not enough for wages? They're paid on credit (cash goes negative), but only once every 3 months. The next time wages are [b]delayed[/b]: people get angry, and a letter offers to take a loan or ask them to be patient.
• From the 3rd day of delay the unhappiest person leaves. Three gone within two weeks and the labor inspectorate [b]shuts the plant[/b] (game over).
• Cash negative for two days or more lowers reputation; sales won't take new orders while you're in debt.
• No tools and no money: a letter offers to buy from the supplier on credit (+10%) or wait.

• Finance → Summary: money and recent transactions.
• By week: a report by item, product cost and margin, a two-week cash forecast (needs an accountant and “Cost accounting”).
• Charts: money, revenue and expenses, market share, mood and reputation by day.

Fire safety, the labor inspectorate, sanitary inspectors, technical supervision, ecologists, the tax office and (for state orders) military acceptance.
• Scheduled ones are announced three days ahead. The inspector walks around the plant and records violations on entering a room, so while he walks you can still fix things.
• The list of requirements is in Events → Inspections; violations are marked red on the map.
• Small businesses (before “Small business”) get a warning instead of a fine for a first violation. Not fixed by the deadline in the order? A double fine.

• In Events → Inspections a red line has “→ how to fix?”: a “What's wrong / How to fix” box with a “Show the spot” button.
• The inspection report has a “How to fix” section.
• The inspector is accompanied by an escort: a safety engineer (15% smaller fines), the shop manager or a foreman.
• A fine can be appealed: a 40% chance, 60% with a lawyer.

A special assessment of working conditions: a lab measures noise, air, light and microclimate at every machine and assigns a class: 2 is acceptable, 3.1–3.3 are hazardous.
• Hazardous workplaces are owed a 4–12% wage supplement and milk.
• The labor inspectorate fines you if no assessment was done.
• Improved the conditions? Order new measurements and the class goes down.

• [b]PPE[/b]: hard hats, goggles, earmuffs, respirators. Newcomers arrive without them, and a kit wears out in about 20 shifts. Put up a [b]PPE cabinet[/b] (Objects → Safety) and supply will restock kits by itself. Without PPE there are 1.5× more injuries.
• With earmuffs noise doesn't irritate; with a respirator, less smoke.
• [b]Hazard milk[/b]: 70 ₽ per person per shift (People → Safety). Not given? Resentment and a fine.

Once every two months: 30% fewer injuries, and the labor inspectorate checks the log if you have 6 or more workers.
It's run by the safety engineer, the shop manager or a foreman, at a board, a safety stand or the “Days without injury” board; people stand in a semicircle.

After every injury a commission finds the causes within three working days.
• If the company is at fault: compensation for the victim and a fine (half with a safety engineer).
• “Blame the worker” is cheaper, but people and the union will remember, and the labor inspectorate will find a hidden injury.
• The “Days without injury” board cuts injuries by 5%.

Free workers run to put it out, many times faster with an extinguisher.
• A [b]fire extinguisher[/b] (2,400 ₽) is needed in every room except toilets and showers; two in hot shops. Fire safety requires it.
• Property insurance covers fire damage.

Injuries come from fatigue, rush jobs, worn machines, darkness, cold and slippery chips or ice.
• The injured person goes on sick leave; a first aid kit nearby shortens it.
• Fewer injuries: PPE, briefings (−30%), a safety engineer (−15%), the “Days without injury” board, light and order.

A completely worn machine breaks down, and the repair is expensive and long. Turn on preventive maintenance, keep a fitter and a setter. A broken machine is listed in Production → Downtime with the reason.

A first aid post: a couch, a medicine cabinet and a sink + a paramedic (the “Social services” step).
• Sick leave after injuries 40% shorter, flu (November to February) rarer.
• Vaccinating the whole staff (600 ₽ per person) means four times fewer cases.

• [b]Mice[/b] appear in very dirty rooms: people are unhappy and the sanitary inspection fines you. Clean up and the mice leave.
• [b]Pigeons[/b] stroll in the yard during the day and sometimes fly into the shop through an open gate.
• The [b]cat[/b] hunts mice and scares pigeons.

The storyteller throws in events: fires, injuries, thefts, defective metal, price jumps, “hot” orders, improvement proposals, weddings, poaching, barter, visits from the governor and a journalist.
• Where a choice is needed, a [b]letter[/b] with options arrives; the game pauses (can be turned off in settings).
• Not decided within the given hours? The default option is chosen.

Town → Overview. Relations grow with care for people (dormitory, lunches, first aid post, kindergarten, House of Culture) and fall with layoffs.
• 60+ brings more candidates, 75+ a 1% lower tax on revenue.
• It's one of the growth roads to the next stage.

A room with bunk beds (two bunks each) and a locker → a “Dormitory” zone. While there are free bunks, out-of-town candidates arrive on Mondays: a bit cheaper, never late, they go “home” to the dorm. Rent: 100 ₽ a day per resident.

The canteen has an industrial stove (powered) and a serving line, and there's a cook on staff. The cook makes portions for everyone (food costs 85 ₽ per portion); a hot lunch gives +9 to mood instead of +6.

• [b]Kindergarten “Little Gear”[/b] (the “Patronage” step): places for workers' children, 6, 12 or 24. Parents are pleased and don't stay home with the child.
• [b]House of Culture “Machine Builder”[/b]: 600,000 ₽ and 15,000 ₽ a week: clubs and holiday concerts.
A cat turns up by itself (sooner if you have a canteen). Put out a [b]bowl[/b] and it stays: petting it is pleasant, and rats stop spoiling consumables. Town → Cat.
On Mondays the plant newspaper comes out (N): plant news, leading workers, veterans, fights and inspections, weather. The “Newspaper” button stays highlighted until the issue is read.
The calendar is compressed: [b]a month is two weeks[/b] (14 days). The game starts in September. There are holidays, summer vacations and a monthly plan. Events → Calendar shows what's ahead.

In winter, frosts down to −15 °C and snow.
• Put up [b]radiators[/b] and a boiler, or the shops get cold: below +15 °C people are chilly, below +6 very cold, work is slower and injuries more common.
• Laborers clear snow with shovels; people slip on ice.
• Flu runs from November to February.

In summer up to +21 °C on average, higher in a heat wave. Above +29 °C indoors people are hot: ventilation helps. Summer is vacation time. In spring farm machinery has twice the orders. Rain and wind are visible on the map.

• The New Year party and New Year holidays (3 days off).
• February 23 and March 8.
• A community cleanup day in April.
• Spring and Labor Day (a day off).
• Machine Builders' Day in September.
With a House of Culture, holiday concerts.

• Camera: WASD or the arrows, the wheel zooms, the middle button drags (and the screen edge, if enabled in settings).
• Left-click selects a person or object; clicking a structure opens its card.
• Right-click or Esc cancels a tool or selection; right-click with a person selected gives an order.
• A person's menu stays above them until it's closed.

• [b]Space[/b]: pause, [b]1/2/3[/b]: speed ×1/×2/×4.
• [b]B[/b]: build, [b]O[/b]: objects, [b]R[/b]: zones (rotates while placing an object), [b]E[/b]: utilities, [b]V[/b]: plan, [b]X[/b]: demolish.
• [b]P[/b]: production, [b]L[/b]: people, [b]K[/b]: crews, [b]F[/b]: finance, [b]M[/b]: management, [b]T[/b]: research.
• [b]G[/b]: goals, [b]C[/b]: events, [b]N[/b]: newspaper, [b]H[/b]: town.
• [b]F1[/b]: this handbook, [b]F3[/b]: frame counter, [b]F5[/b]: quick save, [b]F9[/b]: quick load, [b]Esc[/b]: close or menu.

• F5: quick save, F9: quick load.
• Menu (Esc) → “Save game” / “Load game”: slots with the computer's date and time.
• Each plant has its own autosave; the game saves by itself when you quit.

Menu (Esc) → Settings:
• Volume by category: master, music, machines and tools, ambient sounds, interface.
• [b]Music selection[/b]: by time of day / everything / waltzes only.
• Effects quality (sparks, steam, leaves), frame limit and V-Sync.
• Edge scrolling, pause on an event letter.
• Language: Russian / English.

F3 shows the frames per second in the corner, the frame time, how much of it went to the simulation and how many people are at the plant. Press F3 again to hide it. Lagging? Lower the effects quality in settings.
In the main menu and in “Create a Worker”, F3 shows a diagnostics line: frames per second, frame time (average and worst), nodes, “orphans”, objects, texture memory and video memory. If the menu starts lagging, send a screenshot with this line.
